research.appliedthaumaturge.f_aecore.tit: Examine a device of Applied Energistics.
research.appliedthaumaturge.unlock_energ:
The machines of Applied Energistics convert matter into energy and back again with frightening ease.
I should examine one of these devices closely. If matter can be made digital, perhaps essentia can too.
I am now certain that technology and magic can be combined in a stable and productive way. A new field of study has opened before me.
research.appliedthaumaturge.base_energis:
As both a scientist and an arcane scholar, I have postulated that it must be possible to combine technology and magic in a stable and productive way.
I should study the principles of matter-energy conversion in detail to accomplish this. It is likely there are aspects of Thaumaturgy that can accomplish this, as well as technology capable of doing the same.
This will require extensive study, but I am sure that it will be a worthwhile investment of my time.
research.appliedthaumaturge.digisentia.s:
Having discovered how to distill essentia, it occurs to me that I may be able to store it digitally.
Examining the §lFormation Core§r and §lAnnihilation Core§r I realize that with some minor modifications they could serve as a means to convert essentia to and from a digital format.
However, due to the corrosive nature of certain types of essentia, a layer of quicksilver around the circuitry is required to prevent decay.

§lDiffusion Core§r
The relatively high volatility and immense energy in distilled essentia requires that it first be diffused then digitized. A buffer chamber of some kind will likely be required to hold the diffused essentia.§lCoalescence Core§r
Compresses and binds re-materialized essentia diffusion back into its raw form. A buffer chamber will also likely be needed.
research.appliedthaumaturge.essentia_sto:
Upon inspecting existing digital storage mediums I have concluded that I can in fact store digitized essentia.
By infusing §lCertus Quartz§r with §lSalis Mundus§r, it should gain the ability to store the essentia, which remains remarkably active even in digital form.
I theorize that the higher the concentration of §lSalis Mundus§r, the more it should be able to store, although there are inherent limits as to how much the quartz itself can store.

I have managed to create a storage device capable of storing a small amount of essentia digitally. A warded housing of thaumium and quartz glass keeps the digitized essentia contained. Maybe I could combine multiple components for increased storage?
Maybe I can use some different processing components to combine multiple storage components together.
I can now store a decent amount of essentia digitally by using some calculation processors to allow the components to talk to each other.
Like I did with my previous attempt to get bigger storage components, I can use some high end processors to combine multiple storage components together.
Using another type of processor, I can now store 16x the amount of essentia on a storage component than when I started with my crude storage system.
My current storage needs are not enough. I hope I can still combine storage components to create a larger one while taking up the same space...
I can now store massive amounts of essentia on a storage component, but I feel that this is the limit of the technology.
research.appliedthaumaturge.essentia_bus: Now that I have the components to safely transport essentia with my ME system, I can now work on creating buses for essentia.
I can now make Import, Export, and Storage Buses. They all function exactly like their item counterparts.
research.appliedthaumaturge.essentia_lev: My Essentia Buses move essentia in and out of my network without complaint, but they do so blindly - I have no way to react automatically when a particular aspect runs low, or floods past where I'd like it to. I should adapt the principles behind my ME Level Emitter to watch essentia quantities instead of items.

The Essentia Level Emitter watches a single aspect's stored quantity and emits a redstone signal once it crosses a threshold I set, comparing it as either above or below - exactly like its item counterpart, just tuned to essentia instead.
research.appliedthaumaturge.essentia_ter: While I can now digitize essentia, I have realized this means I can no longer observe the quantities of essentia I have digitalized - an urgent problem.
The ME Essentia Terminal allows me to see all essentia my ME network can access. Additionally, I can insert and extract essentia with phials and jars through it.
research.appliedthaumaturge.wireless_ess: Standing at a terminal to check my essentia reserves is tedious. The wireless terminals of Applied Energistics could surely be attuned to digitized essentia.
By binding my Essentia Terminal into a wireless terminal, I can now watch and manage my essentia from anywhere within range of a wireless access point.
research.appliedthaumaturge.infusion_pro: While being able to manipulate essentia with my ME system has proven invaluable, I am frustrated with the process required for Infusion - I have to extract all my essentia into jars on-site. Perhaps if I could expose my essentia to the Runic Matrix similar to the Essentia Terminal...

Success! The Infusion Provider will expose the entire ME network's essentia to the Infusion process! As a bonus, it also works with my ME Essentia Storage Buses, allowing me to create essentia subnetworks, should I ever need those.
research.appliedthaumaturge.essentia_int: I did, in fact, end up needing those essentia subnetworks - my Infusion Provider trick works, but it is a fragile improvisation. I want a device built for exactly this job: something that lets an Essentia Storage Bus on one ME network see cleanly into another.

The Essentia Interface does precisely that. Point an Essentia Storage Bus at it from another network and the two networks' essentia become visible to each other. It also draws essentia in from any connected tube, and feeds essentia back out to anything that pulls on it harder than a jar would.
research.appliedthaumaturge.arcane_termi: Having to hop back and forth between my ME system and my Arcane Workbench for every craft is getting frustrating. While it is vastly more complex than a mere Crafting Terminal, using the same principles, I should be able to hook my Arcane Workbench into my ME system.

The Arcane Crafting Terminal allows my Arcane Workbench to take full advantage of my ME system. Like a bare workbench, it draws vis only from the aura of the chunk it sits in, and refills its crafting grid and crystals straight from the network.
By binding the principles of the Workbench Charger into an Arcane Charging Card, I can extend the terminal's reach to nearby chunks as well, splitting each draw evenly across the area. The configured chunk radius determines its reach; the default radius of one covers all nine chunks in a 3 by 3 area.
I can also examine stored items without withdrawing them: pick up a Thaumometer onto the cursor and hold it over an item in the terminal's storage display, just as I would in my inventory.
research.appliedthaumaturge.knowledge_co: My Arcane Crafting Terminal saves me countless trips, but every craft still needs my hands. Perhaps the issue is that my machines do not know how to craft - they have not spent hours researching, after all. I should look into ways to give a device a memory of how a recipe is made.

Eureka! I don't need a machine to research - likely an impossible task - I merely need to create something that can remember a craft I've done, and repeat it exactly the same way. A zombie brain is perfect for this - all I have to do is teach the brain the recipe I show it. A single brain can remember up to nine recipes by default; the configured limit determines its capacity.
Should I wish to wipe a brain's memory entirely, a firm squeeze while crouching (Shift + Right-Click) returns the Knowledge Core to a blank state.
research.appliedthaumaturge.arcane_inscr: It appears the undead are not very bright. I've been trying to teach this Knowledge Core how to craft for a while now, yet it hasn't learned anything. I need to find a way to force the Knowledge Core to learn.

Basing my design off of an ME Pattern Encoding Terminal, I have managed to design a kind of terminal that can teach recipes to a Knowledge Core. I simply load the recipe into the grid and inscribe it! If I load a recipe the core already knows, I can erase it from the zombie's memory instead. While a single zombie brain is limited in how many recipes it can remember, zombies are plentiful.
research.appliedthaumaturge.entangled_wa: The engineers of Applied Energistics compress matter into singularities so dense that they bend the very fabric between places. If a pair of silverwood cores were infused around such a singularity, the two might come to share a single reservoir of vis, no matter how far apart they are carried.

To begin the infusion, I place one Silverwood Wand Core on the central pedestal. Six surrounding pedestals each hold one ingredient: a second Silverwood Wand Core, two Fluix Crystals on separate pedestals, two Ender Pearls on separate pedestals, and one Singularity. The Singularity belongs on a surrounding pedestal, not in the center. I leave the other surrounding pedestals empty and activate the Runic Matrix with my wand after completing this research.
The infusion needs 32 Permutatio, 24 Vacuos, 16 Aer, and 16 Praecantatio before altar modifiers. It produces both entangled cores together on the central pedestal, already bound to one another. Any two wands assembled from the same pair share one reservoir of vis, holding as much as a single silverwood wand, across any distance and even between worlds.
I can leave one wand resting on a Recharge Pedestal or my workbench charger and carry the other; whatever vis the resting wand gathers is instantly available to the one in my hand. Cores from different infusions are strangers to each other, so I must take care to keep each pair together.
research.appliedthaumaturge.arcane_assem: While being able to manually craft arcane items with my ME network is very helpful, the true power of ME is its auto-crafting ability. I should look into some way to make a Molecular Assembler able to craft arcane objects.

Everything ought to work - it can get the items, the vis, the essentia crystals, the power. Yet it doesn't even attempt to craft! It seems it simply does not know how. Perhaps a Knowledge Core could teach it.
Once it holds a Knowledge Core, every recipe the core remembers becomes available to my network's auto-crafting. Each Capacity Card unlocks one additional Knowledge Core slot, up to three cores with two cards, storing a total of 27 recipes by default. The configured per-core limit determines the total capacity. It draws vis from the aura of its own chunk, or from nearby chunks as well with an Arcane Charging Card whose reach is set by the configured chunk radius, and Acceleration Cards hasten its work. A linked Vis Relay fills an internal buffer holding up to 150 vis of each primal aspect by default, with its capacity set by configuration. Six horizontal colored bars beside the crafting grid show these stored amounts; hovering a bar reveals its exact contents. The assembler spends buffered relay vis first, then draws any shortfall from an installed wand. If no usable wand is installed, matching essentia crystals cover the remaining requirement. An installed wand that lacks enough vis waits to recharge instead of consuming crystals. Crystal payments increase the aura cost, just as they do at the workbench. If neither source can cover an aspect, crafting waits. An entangled wand lets me replenish that charge through its paired wand elsewhere.
research.appliedthaumaturge.vis_relay_in: A vis relay carries the primal energies of an energized node, yet its reach is limited. My ME network could carry those energies between distant relays, drawing them only when a device needs them. A P2P tunnel and a vis relay should provide the necessary interface.

I place a Vis Relay Interface on an ME cable facing a linked vis relay. Sneak-right-clicking the interface with a Memory Card records it as the source. I can then right-click another interface on the same active ME network to make it a receiver. Relays near the receiving cable can draw vis from it and supply their usual consumers. Right-clicking my Arcane Crafting Terminal or Arcane Assembler with the recorded card instead lets it steadily recharge the wand in its wand slot, even while its interface is closed and the assembler is idle. The assembler fills its own six primal vis buffers before recharging an idle wand. Buffered vis is used first for crafting, followed by wand vis; crystals are used only without a usable wand.
Each interface needs a channel. The source spends 4 AE power per successful draw; vis remains in the original node until a consumer requests it. Source and receiving chunks must remain loaded. Separate ME networks cannot share the link, and a receiving interface cannot serve as another link's source.
A blank Memory Card clears a receiver, terminal, or assembler's link. Sneak-right-clicking an interface records it as a source again. Changing a link does not move any vis into storage cells.
research.appliedthaumaturge.portable_ess: My essentia cells hold a vast collection of aspects, but I must return to a terminal whenever I need them. Combining a cell with an ME Chest and a rechargeable energy cell should let me carry that collection with me.

Portable Essentia Cells let me access stored aspects directly from my inventory. Right-clicking the cell opens its terminal, where phials and jars can deposit or withdraw essentia. I can also right-click a filled container onto a cell in my inventory to empty it into storage.
The four tiers each hold up to twelve aspect types, with half the byte capacity of the corresponding ordinary cell, just like AE2's portable cells. A Charger replenishes the internal battery, and Energy Cards extend its charge. Inverter, Equal Distribution, and Void Cards support the usual cell configuration.
I can upgrade a portable cell without losing its contents, charge, or upgrades. Sneak-right-clicking an empty cell disassembles it and returns its components. Portable cells also work in ME Drives and Chests.
